title: Bonus Game Weighting in Canada: How Wagering Really Counts
excerpt: Game weighting decides how fast a Canadian casino bonus clears. Here is how the percentages work, which games count, and how to avoid losing a bonus by accident.
author: David Andersen
bodyHtml:
Bonus game weighting is the single most misunderstood line in a Canadian casino bonus's terms and conditions, and it is the reason plenty of players think they cleared a wagering requirement when the casino says they did not. The headline offer tells you the requirement — 35x the bonus, say. The weighting table tells you how much of each dollar you bet actually counts toward it. Ignore that table and you can grind for hours while barely moving the bar.

This guide explains how weighting works at Canadian online casinos, why table games are treated so differently from slots, and how to plan a bonus so you are not caught out by a rule buried on page three of the terms.

What game weighting actually means

When a casino sets a wagering requirement, it is asking you to place a certain volume of bets before bonus funds convert to withdrawable cash. A $100 bonus with a 35x requirement means $3,500 in qualifying wagers. The word doing the work there is qualifying.

Weighting assigns each game category a percentage that determines how much of your stake counts. A typical Canadian casino table looks something like this:

  • Slots: 100% — a $1 spin contributes $1 toward the requirement.
  • Video poker: often 10-20%, sometimes excluded entirely.
  • Roulette: commonly 10-25%, with some casinos excluding it altogether.
  • Blackjack: frequently 5-10%, and excluded more often than any other table game.
  • Live dealer games: usually 10% or less, sometimes zero.
  • Baccarat, craps and sic bo: typically 5-10% or excluded.

Do the arithmetic on the worst case and the picture is stark. That same $3,500 requirement, played on a blackjack table weighted at 5%, means placing $70,000 in bets. No sane bankroll survives that, which is exactly the point: casinos weight low-house-edge games down because clearing a bonus on them would be close to a break-even proposition for the player.

Why the percentages differ so much

Weighting is a house-edge calculation, not an arbitrary preference. A typical online slot holds somewhere in the region of 4-6% of every dollar wagered. A blackjack player using correct basic strategy faces a house edge under 1%, and a player betting red and black alternately on roulette can grind through volume with very little expected loss.

If every game counted at 100%, the cheapest way to clear a bonus would be to bet large amounts on the lowest-edge game available, take a small expected loss, and withdraw the difference. Weighting closes that door. The percentages roughly equalise the casino's expected return across game types over the life of a bonus.

This is also why you will see rules that go beyond weighting — bans on covering more than a set percentage of the roulette table, maximum bet limits while a bonus is active, and exclusions on so-called low-risk play. Those clauses exist to stop the same arbitrage from a different angle. If you want to understand how the underlying maths differs between games, our blackjack strategy guide and roulette guide lay out the house edge on each bet type.

The rules that void bonuses

Weighting decides how fast you clear. A separate set of clauses decides whether you clear at all. The most common bonus-killers at Canadian casinos are:

Maximum bet while wagering

Almost every bonus caps the stake you may place on a single spin or hand while a wagering requirement is outstanding — commonly $5 to $8. Exceed it once, even accidentally, and many operators will void the bonus and any winnings derived from it. Autoplay with a bet size set before you claimed the bonus is a classic way to trip this.

Excluded games

An excluded game contributes nothing, and at some casinos playing one at all is a terms breach rather than simply a zero-weighted wager. Progressive jackpot slots and certain high-RTP titles are excluded more often than players expect.

Feature buys

Buying a bonus round is banned during wagering at a growing number of Canadian sites, because feature buys concentrate variance in a way that favours the player attempting to clear a large requirement quickly.

Time limits

Requirements usually expire in seven to thirty days. A generous bonus with a seven-day window can be functionally impossible to clear at a stake size your bankroll supports.

How to plan a bonus around weighting

Start by converting the offer into real numbers before you deposit. Multiply the bonus by the requirement, then divide by the weighting of the games you actually intend to play. If the resulting turnover is more than roughly ten to fifteen times your deposit, ask whether the bonus is worth the constraints it puts on your session.

Then think about volatility. Clearing a large requirement on a high-variance slot is a coin flip: you either hit a feature early and cruise, or your balance evaporates well before the turnover is met. Medium-volatility slots with a decent published RTP are usually the better vehicle, because they let you survive long enough to actually reach the finish line. Our explainer on how online slots work covers volatility and RTP in more depth.

Finally, decide whether you want a bonus at all. Plenty of experienced Canadian players decline welcome offers entirely and play with cash, because unrestricted funds can be withdrawn at any moment and carry no maximum bet rule. A bonus is a trade: extra funds in exchange for control over how you play. Whether that trade is good depends on how you like to play, not on the size of the headline number.

Reading a weighting table before you claim

Weighting information is not always in the bonus terms themselves. At many casinos it lives in a general terms page, a dedicated bonus policy, or a help-centre article, and it can differ between the welcome offer and later reload promotions at the same site. If you cannot find it in under two minutes, ask support to confirm the weighting for the specific games you plan to play, and keep the reply.

Operators that publish a clear, current weighting table on the same page as the offer are, in our experience, the ones least likely to spring a surprise at withdrawal time. It is one of the small signals we weigh when scoring sites in our Canadian casino reviews, alongside payout speed and the quality of the complaints process.

The short version

Game weighting is not a trick, but it is not advertised either. Treat the percentage table as part of the offer rather than fine print, convert the requirement into the turnover you will personally face, and check the maximum bet rule before your first spin. Do those three things and bonuses become a modest, predictable extra rather than a source of disputes.

You must be 19+ (18+ in some provinces) to gamble in Canada. If gambling stops being fun, free confidential help is available in every province.
